title_en: The Winter Melon Too Big for the Gate
note_en: A verb plus 不出 is a potential complement meaning "can't get it out": 怎么也搬不出院门 "no matter what, they couldn't move it out through the gate." Put 得 in place of 不 and you get the positive, 搬得出 "can move it out." English needs "can't" plus a verb plus a particle; Chinese packs the ability into the middle of the verb phrase, and 怎么也 + negative adds "no matter how hard they tried."
